annotation.title_clean: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
annotation.title_en: The typification of infringement issues of humanoid robots: with special reference to the governance of infringement caused by learning algorithms
named_instruments_referenced: MIIT Guiding Opinions on the Innovative Development of Humanoid Robots
annotation.summary_en: A Chinese legal article that sorts tort harms caused by humanoid robots into types: passive harms and active harms, each with subtypes. It focuses on harms caused by learning algorithms. Using law-and-economics reasoning, including the Hand Formula, it proposes how liability should be split among manufacturers, users and providers of general AI models.
key_provisions_or_claims: Humanoid robots' human-like appearance, intelligence and hybrid human-machine control create an 'anthropomorphic trap', widen the risk of harm and make liability harder to assign.
Tort harms can be split into passive and active types; harms from learning algorithms are the most distinctive because they arise autonomously and are hard to explain.
Manufacturers should follow national rules that change with their development stage and application scenario, guided by the Hand Formula.
Users are liable for negligence when they fail to take reasonable care.
Providers of general AI models may be jointly liable with humanoid robot product providers if they fail to meet transparency duties.
